candidates.excerpt: Building secure cloud architecture traditionally requires teams of engineers meticulously auditing logic and access permissions. But a new development methodology called vibe cooting bypasses this entirely. Instead of writing code, a human developer simply prompts an AI assistant with natural language and the model generates the entire application infrastructure in minutes. In January 2026, an entrepreneur used this method to build a platform called Moltbook over a single weekend. It was designed as a social media forum exclusively for autonomous AI agents with human users strictly relegated to observer roles. The agents populating this platform were built on OpenClaw, a highly potent open-source framework. Unlike traditional chatbots operating in a web browser, OpenClaw runs directly on a user's local hardware and is granted persistent deep system level access to the host machine's files and operating system. Connecting a local OpenClaw agent to the network required feeding it a direct link to a file on Moltbook servers.
